上海，1931年2月10日。

副总监，
（刑事及特别部门）。

关于亨兹与巴尔公司：佣金代理商，
1931年2月1日《字林西报》上的广告。

现就今日收到详情的上述广告，针对以下几点出具意见：

1. 广告商发送此类广告，若有任何罪行，构成了什么罪行？

2. 报社刊登此类广告，若有任何罪行，构成了什么罪行？

另外——

3. 亨兹与巴尔公司经营此类业务，若有任何罪行，构成了什么罪行？

1. 首先，该广告可被解释为向公众发出的一般性邀请，邀请公众前往中央商场100号查询博彩事宜，并将其视为可以下注的场所。因此，已构成违反《1874年博彩法》第3条的罪行。该条款规定：

page_data.en:
-2-

reads:

"Where any letter, circular, telegram, pla-
card, handbill, card, or advertisement is sent,
exhibited, or published -

(1) Whereby it is made to appear that any person,
either in the united kingdom or elsewhere, will
on application give information or advice for the
purpose of or with respect to any such bet or
wager, or any such event or contingency as is
mentioned in the principal act, or will make on
behalf of any other person any such bet or wager
as is mentioned in the principal act; or

(2) With intent to induce any person to apply to
any house, office, room, or place, or to any person,
with the view of obtaining information or advice
for the purpose of any such bet or wager or with
respect to any such event or contingency as is
mentioned in the principal act; or

(3) Inviting any person to make or take any share
in or in connection with any such bet or wager;

every person sending, exhibiting, or publishing,
or causing the same to be sent, exhibited, or
published, shall be subject to the penalties pro-
vided in the seventh section of the principal
act with respect to offences under that section."

The principal act referred to is the Betting Act
1853, section 7 of which provides for a penalty of £30
imprisonment, with or without hard labour for a term not
exceeding two months.

In the case of Hawke & Mackenzie (1902), 2 K. B. 225,
it was held that an advertisement relating to either of
the purposes mentioned in the Betting Act 1853, section 1,
namely, (1) that of keeping a place for the purpose of
betting with persons resorting thereto, and (2) that of
keeping
page_data.zh:
-2-

内容如下：

“凡发送、展示或出版任何信件、通告、电报、海报、传单、卡片或广告——

(1) 致使显示任何人，无论在英国本土或其他地方，将根据申请提供信息或建议，以用于或涉及主法案中提及的任何此类赌注或打赌，或任何此类事件或偶然事故；或将代表任何其他人进行主法案中提及的任何此类赌注或打赌；或

(2) 意图诱使任何人向任何房屋、办公室、房间或场所，或向任何人提出申请，以期获得用于任何此类赌注或打赌的目的，或关于主法案中提及的任何此类事件或偶然事故的信息或建议；或

(3) 邀请任何人进行或参与任何此类赌注或打赌的全部或部分；

每一发送、展示或出版，或导致其被发送、展示或出版的人，均应受到主法案第七节中针对该节下罪行所规定的处罚。”

所指的主法案是《1853年赌博法》，其第七节规定罚款30英镑，并处不超过两个月的监禁，可附加或不附加苦役。

在 Hawke & Mackenzie (1902), 2 K. B. 225 一案中，裁定涉及《1853年赌博法》第一节中提及的任一目的的广告均为非法，即：(1) 为与前往该处的人员进行赌博而保留场所的目的，以及 (2) 为保留

page_data.en:
-3-

keeping a place for the purpose of receiving deposits
and bets, was illegal. It was also decided that the
publication of an advertisement shewing that information
or advice will be given relative to any coupon competition
on any game or sport in which money was to be sent, and
which constituted an offence under the Betting Act 1853,
section 4, was an offence under the Betting Act 1874,
section 3.

The latter decision appears to cover what is called
the "Football Pool", but information should be obtained
on this.

2. It appears that the newspaper would also be
guilty of an offence under the Betting Act 1874, section 3,
although no decided case on the point can be found. As
far as can be remembered, the advertisements of commission
agents at home are generally confined to the name, descrip-
tion, address and telephone number; in no case would the
particular race and odds given with an invitation for
further enquiries be given.

3. Although there is a Scottish case (Scott v.
Renton (1907) S. C. (J) 88, deciding there is no need that
there should be any invitation to resort to any named
address for the purpose of betting, or that bets should
be accepted there for an offence to be committed under the
Betting Act 1874, section 3, it is thought that particulars
of
page_data.zh:
-3-

为接收存款和赌注而保留场所的目的。还裁定，发布表明将提供有关任何需汇款参与的赛事或体育项目的优惠券竞赛的信息或建议的广告，构成《1853年赌博法》第四节下的罪行，同时也构成《1874年赌博法》第三节下的罪行。

后一项裁决似乎涵盖了所谓的“足球彩池”（Football Pool），但应就此获取更多信息。

2. 报纸似乎也将犯有《1874年赌博法》第三节下的罪行，尽管未找到关于此点的已决案例。据回忆，国内佣金代理人的广告通常仅限于名称、描述、地址和电话号码；在任何情况下，都不会列出特定赛马及赔率并邀请进一步查询。

3. 虽然有一苏格兰案例（Scott v. Renton (1907) S. C. (J) 88）裁定，无需邀请人们前往任何指定地址进行赌博，也无需在该处接受赌注，即可构成《1874年赌博法》第三节下的罪行，但认为在采取任何行动之前，应获取

page_data.en:
-4-
of the place and proceedings therein should be obtained
before any action is taken.
As Messrs. Hinds & Barr do not appear to be on
the telephone, then people must either resort thereto for
the purpose of making bets or forward their bets by
letter. In either case, there is every possibility ready
money will be taken or sent as credit accounts are opened
for responsible residents only. If that is so, then an
offence has been committed under the Betting Act 1853,
section 3, which reads as follows:
"Any person who being the owner or occupier
of any house, office, room or other place, or a
person using the same, shall open, keep or use
the same for the purposes hereinbefore mentioned,
or either of them; and any person who being the
owner or occupier of any house, room, office, or
other place shall knowingly and wilfully permit
the same to be opened, kept, or used by any other
person for the purposes aforesaid, or either of
them; and any person having the care or management
of or in any manner assisting in conducting the
business of any house, office, room, or place opened,
kept, or used for the purposes aforesaid, or either
of them, shall, on summary conviction thereof before
any two justices of the peace, be liable to forfeit
and pay such penalty, not exceeding one hundred pounds,
as shall be adjudged by such justices, and may be
further adjudged by such justices to pay such costs
attending such conviction as to the said justices shall
seem reasonable; and on the non-payment of such penalty
and costs, or in the first instance if to the said
justices it shall seem fit, may be committed to the
common gaol or house of correction, with or without
hard labour, for any time not exceeding six calendar
months."
The purposes aforesaid are contained in Section 1
of the Act, and have already been summarised. In short,
it
page_data.zh:
-4-

关于该地点及其中活动情况的详细信息。
由于 Hinds & Barr 先生们似乎没有安装电话，那么人们必须要么前往该处以进行赌博，要么通过信件发送赌注。在这两种情况下，极有可能收取或接收现金，因为信用账户仅向负责任的居民开放。如果是这样，则已犯有《1853年赌博法》第三节下的罪行，该节规定如下：
“任何作为任何房屋、办公室、房间或其他场所的所有者或占用者，或使用该场所的人，开设、保留或使用该场所以用于上述目的，或其中任一目的；以及任何作为任何房屋、房间、办公室或其他场所的所有者或占用者，明知且故意允许该场所被任何其他人开设、保留或用于上述目的，或其中任一目的；以及任何负责管理或以任何方式协助经营为上述目的，或其中任一目的而开设、保留或使用的任何房屋、办公室、房间或场所的业务的人，经两名治安法官简易程序定罪后，应没收并支付由该等法官判处的不超过一百英镑的罚款，并可由该等法官进一步判处支付该等法官认为合理的因该定罪产生的费用；如不支付该等罚款和费用，或者如果该等法官认为适当，在初次判决时，可被投入普通监狱或感化院，附加或不附加苦役，期限不超过六个日历月。”
上述目的载于该法第一节，并已在前文总结。简而言之，它

page_data.en:
-5-

it was decided in the case of Traynor v. Macpherson (1914)
S. C. (J). 174, that no offence was committed when no cus-
tomers resorted to the premises occupied by the bookmaker,
but communicated by letter, telegram or telephone, and
paid no deposit when the bet was made, but accounts were
rendered weekly and balances remitted. If any of these
contingencies are not complied with, then an offence is
committed.

    If it is proposed to take action, then it is suggested:
    (1) That someone be sent to the place to make a bet
and pay a deposit, and also to make enquiries with regard
to the "Football Pool" and obtain a coupon.
    (2) That watch be kept to ascertain the number of
people resorting there, and also if possible the number of
letters delivered. The person sent to the office might be
able to give some idea of the conduct of the business.
    (3) If enquiries justify it, a search warrant should
be obtained and executed after a number of people have
visited the premises.

    It is thought the above will be sufficient guide for
the time being; amplification can be made, if necessary,
by reference to various authorities.

Sean
ARP
RW/J.

Rhodes.
Assistant Municipal Advocate
page_data.zh:
-5-

在 Traynor v. Macpherson (1914) S. C. (J). 174 一案中裁定，当没有顾客前往庄家占用的处所，而是通过信件、电报或电话进行沟通，且在下注时未支付押金，而是每周结算账单并汇寄余额时，不构成犯罪。如果这些条件有任何一项未得到满足，则构成犯罪。

    如果拟采取行动，建议：
    (1) 派人前往该处下注并支付押金，并就“足球彩池”进行查询并获取优惠券。
    (2) 进行监视，以确定前往该处的人数，以及如果可能的话，投递的信件数量。派往办公室的人员或许能提供一些关于业务运作情况的概念。
    (3) 如果调查证明有必要，应在多人访问该处所后，取得并执行搜查令。

    认为上述内容足以作为目前的指导；如有必要，可通过参考各种权威资料进行补充。

Sean
ARP
RW/J.

Rhodes.

for responsible residents only. If that is so, then an
offence has been committed under the Betting Act 1853,
section 3, which reads as follows:
"Any person who being the owner or occupier
of any house, office, room or other place, or a
person using the same, shall open, keep or use
the same for the purposes hereinbefore mentioned,
or either of them; and any person who being the
owner or occupier of any house, room, office, or
other place shall knowingly and wilfully permit
the same to be opened, kept, or used by any other
person for the purposes aforesaid, or either of
them; and any person having the care or management
of or in any manner assisting in conducting the
business of any house, office, room, or place opened,
kept, or used for the purposes aforesaid, or either
of them, shall, on summary conviction thereof before
any two justices of the peace, be liable to forfeit
and pay such penalty, not exceeding one hundred pounds,
as shall be adjudged by such justices, and may be
further adjudged by such justices to pay such costs
attending such conviction as to the said justices shall
seem reasonable; and on the non-payment of such penalty
and costs, or in the first instance if to the said
justices it shall seem fit, may be committed to the
common gaol or house of correction, with or without
hard labour, for any time not exceeding six calendar
months."
The purposes aforesaid are contained in section 1
of the Act, and have already been summarised. In short,
18

关于该地点及其中活动情况的详细信息。
由于 Hinds & Barr 先生们似乎没有安装电话，那么人们必须要么前往该处以进行赌博，要么通过信件发送赌注。在这两种情况下，极有可能收取或接收现金，因为信用账户仅向负责任的居民开放。如果是这样，则已犯有《1853年赌博法》第三节下的罪行，该节规定如下：
“任何作为任何房屋、办公室、房间或其他场所的所有者或占用者，或使用该场所的人，开设、保留或使用该场所以用于上述目的，或其中任一目的；以及任何作为任何房屋、房间、办公室或其他场所的所有者或占用者，明知且故意允许该场所被任何其他人开设、保留或用于上述目的，或其中任一目的；以及任何负责管理或以任何方式协助经营为上述目的，或其中任一目的而开设、保留或使用的任何房屋、办公室、房间或场所的业务的人，经两名治安法官简易程序定罪后，应没收并支付由该等法官判处的不超过一百英镑的罚款，并可由该等法官进一步判处支付该等法官认为合理的因该定罪产生的费用；如不支付该等罚款和费用，或者如果该等法官认为适当，在初次判决时，可被投入普通监狱或感化院，附加或不附加苦役，期限不超过六个日历月。”
上述目的载于该法第一节，并已在前文总结。简而言之，

it was decided in the case of Raynor v. Stephenson (1914;
.. J. (J) 174, that no offence was committed when no cus-
tomers resorted to the premises occupied by the bookmaker,
but communicated by letter, telegram or telephone, and
paid no deposit when the bet was made, but accounts were
rendered weekly and balances remitted. If any of these
continuances are not complied with, then an offence is
committed.

If it is proposed to take action, then it is suggested:
(1) that someone be sent to the place to make a bet
and pay a deposit, and also to make enquiries with regard
to the "Football Pool" and obtain a coupon.
(2) that watch be kept to ascertain the number of
people resorting there, and also if possible the number of
letters delivered. The person sent to the office might be
able to give some idea of the conduct of the business.
(3) If enquiries justify it, a search warrant should
be obtained and executed after a number of people have
visited the premises.

It is thought the above will be sufficient guide for
the time being; amplification can be made, if necessary,
by reference to various authorities.

Assistant Municipal Advocate

在雷纳诉斯蒂芬森案（Raynor v. Stephenson，1914年；.. J. (J) 174）中裁定，若没有顾客前往占屋者（bookmaker）所占据的处所，而是通过信件、电报或电话进行联络，且在投注时不支付定金，而是每周结算账目并汇寄余额，则不构成犯罪。若上述任何持续条件未被遵守，则构成犯罪。

如拟采取行动，建议如下：
(1) 派人前往该处进行投注并支付定金，同时就“足球彩池”（Football Pool）一事进行查询并获取一张息票（coupon）。

(3) 如果调查证明有此必要，应在多人访问该处所后，申请并执行搜查令。

FOOTBALL POOL
Something new to Shanghai---
but England's latest craze

Running simultaneously with our weekly coupons, we are inaugurating in Shanghai the first "FOOTBALL
POOL" in the Far East.
A "FOOTBALL POOL" is a selection, in this case, of 40 matches from English & Scottish soccer, from which
the competitor has to forecast any 8 results, placing on his selection any stake between $1 to $10.—
From the gross investments, the organisers deduct 10 per cent., and the balance is divided between
the successful competitors—pro rata to their investment.
In the event of no competitor forecasting the correct results, the pool will then be carried over to the
following week and added to that weeks total for division.
This being the first venture of this nature in Shanghai, we are guaranteeing a return of at least 18
to 1 to any successful competitor.
When the popularity of this Pool has been proved, we intend to organize several pools of various
Combinations, the competitor then having a choice of several selections.
Documents to hand from our London Agents, show that the demand for this type of speculation is
enormous, and for matches played on the 27th ultimo, one pool paid to a successful competitor the odds of
3024 to 1.

足球彩池
上海的新鲜事物——
却是英国最新的狂热

与我们每周的息票同步运行，我们在上海 inaugurating（ inaugurate，此处意为创办/启动）远东第一个“足球彩池”。
“足球彩池”是从英格兰和苏格兰足球比赛中选出40场比赛，参赛者需预测其中任意8场比赛的结果，并在其选择上投入1至10美元之间的任何赌注。
从总投注额中，组织者扣除10%，余额按比例分配给成功的参赛者——根据其投注金额比例分配。
如果没有参赛者预测出正确结果，彩池将结转至下一周，并加入该周的总额中进行分配。
鉴于这是上海此类性质的首次尝试，我们保证向任何成功的参赛者提供至少18比1的回报。
当此彩池的受欢迎程度得到证实后，我们打算组织多种组合形式的彩池，届时参赛者将有多种选择。
我方伦敦代理人提供的文件显示，对此类投机活动的需求巨大，在上月27日进行的比赛中，有一个彩池向一名成功参赛者支付了3024比1的赔率。

The position in this matter is that evidence has 
been obtained that on the 10th October 1932 Mesers. Hinds & Barr 
accepted cash sums for bets on horse races from two members of 
the Municipal Police. The transactions were separate, but 
apparently the seconi teok place immediately after the first. 

Section 1 of the Betting Act 1853 provides that "ne 
houge, office room or other place shall be opened kept or used 
for the purpose of ......... betting with persons resorting there- 
to: or for the purpose of any money or valuable thing being 
received by or on behalf of such owner ........ for any agreenent 
express or implied, to pay or give therefor any money or valuable 
thing on any event or contingency of or relating to any horse 
race eto." 

B Section 3 provides that any person who, being the 

| owner or oceupier of any house office room or other place, or 
person using the same, shall open keep or use the seme fer the 
parpeses mentioned above shall be liable to a penalty net execed- 
img £100". By section 4 any person ete. who accepts money on: 


contingencies as mentioned above ig liable to a fine not 
exceeding £50. By section 5 any money received by such person 
can be recovered by the bettor with costs. 

We are unable to fini any actual instance of a 
prosecution under thig Act in China; nevertheless at various 
times the Vagrancy Act, Geming House Act 1854 and other Gaming 
Actes have been held by the Court to be applicable to British 
sebdjects in China, and we see no reason to suppose that the 
Betting Act 1853 would not be held to be enforceable. 

feo independent offences are created by Section 1 
of the statute, firstly that of keeping a place for the purpose 
of betting with persons resorting thereto, and secondly that | 
of keeping a place for the purpose of receiving deposits on bets. 
In the ease of Boma v. Plum (1894 1 Q.B. 169) it was held that 
these offenses were separate and that a eonviction eould be 
obtained for the first ef these offenses without proving the 
actual receipt of amy money. 

The gist of doth offences is the keeping of a place 
for the purpose of betting or reeeiving deposits for bets, ani 
it has been held in one ease that proof of the receipt of a bet 
on one occasion is not sufficient to justify a convietion under 
section 3. It is certainly desirable, if possible, that a 
eonviction should be obtained on both of the above counts, anf 


if Messrs. Hinds & Barr are openly accepting eash bets it should 
not be difficult to obtain clear evidence of this. 

As regards establishing that the premises are used 
for the purpose of betting, we should like to have copies of the 
advertisements inserted by Messrs. Hinfis & Barr in the press or 
circulars sent out by them to prospective customers (the writer 
believes that he received such a circular some time ago but 
threw it away; presumably, however, it should not be difficult 
to obtain other examples). 

We think also that considerably more than two 
inatanses should be obtained of the acceptance of cash bets. 

If other persons who are not menbders of the Police, ean be 
found who are willing to come forward and give evidence that 
they have had cash betting transactiong so much the better. 

If it is not considered advisable to approach outside persons 
as to this, we suggest that not less than 8 or 10 instanees of 
the aeseptance of eagh bets should be obtained over a peried of, 
eay, two weeks. 

Corrodoration of bets is not particularly necessary, 
as we do not imagine that the reeeipts will be disputed. Yor
